label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Monday 30 Nov at Embakasi: casuals' pay, notes for Brian

Brian,

Thank you for taking this. Read this on Sunday, and keep it on your phone Monday. I've kept it to what you need.

**1. What actually happened with Friday's pay**

The facts, plain, so you can say them plainly:

- Finance sent the bank the casuals' payment file on Friday as usual. That's 212 people.
- The bank upgraded its system on 25 November and changed the file format. Our file used the old format. One column had a reference that was too long, so the bank rejected the whole file at 1:52pm. Nobody was paid. No money left our account and none went missing.
- The rejection alert went to an old finance mailbox. Kevin only saw it after 5pm. By then the bank's cut-off had passed, so the file could not be resent Friday.
- On Saturday morning the MD approved paying everyone through M-Pesa bulk instead of the bank.

This is our mistake, not theirs. Finance missed the alert, and the company didn't keep up with the bank's change. The guys came to work, did the job, and weren't paid on the day we promised. Please don't go in defensive. Don't blame the bank to get us off the hook. The bank changed a format; we were the ones who didn't catch it. If you open by owning it, half the heat goes out of the room.

**2. When the money lands**

Kevin's realistic estimate is **money on phones Monday by 11am**. He has told me he won't promise earlier, and you shouldn't either.

For the 198 people whose numbers Peninah has confirmed, 11am is the target. It is not a guarantee.

For the **14 people Peninah couldn't reach** (mostly the new loaders from the Athi River intake), they cannot be paid until they give her a correct number. Peninah will be at Embakasi from **7:30** with the printed list. Once she has their numbers, their payments go out after that, so later than the others. Tell them this honestly. Don't let them think they're in the 11am batch.

**3. What the MD has approved (you can promise these)**

These are confirmed in writing by NW, so say them with confidence:

- Everyone is paid in full through M-Pesa on Monday.
- **KES 500 per head for Monday lunch and fare**, for every casual on the affected list. It comes in the same M-Pesa payment.
- **M-Pesa charges are paid by the company.** Nobody gets less than their full pay because of the switch.
- Anyone who wants a printed payslip can get one from Peninah. She's bringing the laptop.
- An apology from management, in person. NW asked that it come from you since I'm travelling. Say it in your own words, early, and mean it.

**4. What you must NOT promise**

- **No exact time we can't keep.** Remember Mombasa 2024. The supervisor told the casuals "by lunch", the money came at 4pm, and half the shift sat down. I never want that again. If you say "11am" and it lands at 11:40, we're back where we started, only worse.

  What I'd say instead: "The payment is being sent this morning. Finance is working to have it on your phones by 11. At 11 I'll come back here myself and tell you exactly where it is." That commits you to an update, which you can keep, rather than a deadline, which you can't fully control.
- Don't say "tomorrow" or "soon". Joseph says the guys remember management saying "tomorrow" for three days last time. Use specifics only.
- Don't promise anything beyond the list in section 3, like extra compensation or that this "will never happen again". If they ask what we're changing, say finance has already fixed the format and the alert problem, and HR will follow up with them this week.
- **No threats about contracts, jobs or future shifts.** Not even a hint. The procedure says so (more in section 6), and it would blow the whole thing up anyway.

**5. Ouma: talk to him first, privately**

Joseph tells me Ouma and two others are telling people not to load the Kisumu trucks until they see money. Ouma is loud, but he's not a bad man. He has four kids and rent due on the 1st, like a lot of them. He's angry for real reasons.

Before you address the whole group, find him early, ideally between 5:30 and 6, with Joseph if that helps. Take him aside and talk to him properly:

- Apologise to him directly first, before you ask him for anything.
- Tell him exactly what's in sections 2 and 3: the time, the lunch and fare money, no charges deducted.
- Be straight about the problem. The trucks must leave at 9, and the money won't be visible on phones by then. Don't pretend otherwise. He'll respect it more.
- Ask him what would make it possible for his group to load. Maybe it's you standing with them at 11. Maybe it's seeing Peninah's list with their names and amounts. Maybe it's something else. Listen before you answer.
- If he agrees to help, let him say it to the group himself. That counts for more than anything coming from you.

Then talk to the whole group, around 6 when the shift starts. Lead with the apology, then the facts, then what's approved, then the 11am update promise.

**6. If Ouma's group still refuses to load**

The Kisumu trucks have to leave by 9 or we miss the offloading slot at the mill. So decide your fallback before you arrive, not at 8:45.

Our procedure (Casual workers: pay and grievance procedure, v3, in this folder) says:

- A work stoppage is handled by **Operations and HR together**.
- **No one is dismissed or threatened with dismissal on the day.**

With me travelling, "HR together" means me on WhatsApp until I board, and on the phone once I land. Peninah will be on site from 7:30 for anything to do with the list and the payments. Don't handle a stoppage on your own if you can help it. Bring me in.

If they won't load:

- Stay calm, and stay with them. Don't walk off and don't argue in front of the group.
- Don't pressure anyone, and don't single anyone out. If some guys choose to load, fine. But don't play them against the others, and don't pull in people from elsewhere in a way that looks like you're replacing the group. We'll still have to work with everyone on Tuesday.
- Nobody who sits down is penalised or threatened on Monday. Write down who, what time, and what was said. HR will deal with it calmly later in the week.
- Keep your word on the 11am update whatever happens with the trucks.
- On the trucks: it might be worth calling the mill early Monday, or even Sunday, to ask what flexibility there is on the slot, just in case. That's your call, you know the mill better than I do.

If it gets heated beyond talking, step back, get Joseph to help keep things calm, and call me.

**7. Timeline Monday**

- 4:30: I'm up. WhatsApp me any time.
- 5:30: You at the depot.
- 5:30–6:00: Ouma, privately.
- ~6:00: Whole group: apology, facts, what's approved.
- ~6:30: I board the KQ 7:05 to Entebbe. **If anything changes before then, WhatsApp me before I board.** After that I'm off the phone until I land, around 8:20. Then I'm reachable again, though I'm in onboarding in Kampala most of the day.
- 7:30: Peninah arrives with the list. The 14 go to her.
- 9:00: Kisumu trucks out.
- 11:00: You go back to the group with an update, whatever it is. If anything is late, check with Kevin before you go out so you have real facts to give them.

**8. People**

- Kevin (finance): payment status on Monday morning. Ask him, not me, for where the batch is.
- Peninah (payroll): the list, the 14 numbers, payslips.
- Joseph (shift supervisor): knows the mood on the floor, and he's tried hard to keep it calm. Use him.
- Me: WhatsApp until about 6:30, then after I land.

Six years, Brian. You know how to talk to these guys better than most. Own it, be specific, don't promise what we can't keep, and come back at 11. Call me.

Achieng
